title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey, December 2026 — the pair's half whose collection window actually spans the 12-11 cliff, 8:30 a.m. ET
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events?release=manufacturing-business-outlook-survey — the Philadelphia Fed's own filtered release calendar, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 131,096 bytes) by this event's own never-assessed initial research. Its embedded structured data enumerates the FULL 2026 MBOS schedule, thirteen rows including verbatim 'December Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey | Dec 17 2026 | 8:30 a.m.' — so this date is now READ from the primary, replacing the rule-reproduced estimate the proposal that filed this id could only derive (the MBOS landing page's Release Calendar panel publishes only the next two releases, and on 2026-09-09 those were Sep 17 and Oct 15). Corroborated by the bank's own published cadence rule, philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/regional-economic-analysis/mbos-faqs (HTTP 200, 55,928 bytes, fetched direct 2026-09-09): 'We usually publish the results at 8:30 a.m. ET on the third Thursday of each month, barring holidays.' December 2026's Thursdays are 3/10/17/24, third = 17. All thirteen enumerated 2026 rows are third Thursdays at 8:30 a.m., so rule and enumeration agree on twelve of twelve monthly observations rather than on the two the landing page happens to show. Filed estimate on the same two counts every sibling regional-survey entry records, NEITHER of which is doubt about the date: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the one proposal that existed for this id (proposals/philly-fed-mfg-2026-12-17.from-empire-state-mfg-2026-12-15.json, filed 2026-09-09 by the Empire State lane) and then discharged BOTH tasks that proposal explicitly assigned to whoever wrote this file. (a) The date is no longer rule-reproduced: the bank's filtered calendar endpoint enumerates December 17 directly. (b) The collection window is no longer inherited from a sibling's inference: the Philadelphia Fed publishes it as a rule, twice and identically — mbos-methodology and mbos-faqs (both HTTP 200, fetched direct 2026-09-09) read 'Typically, we collect responses over an eight-day period that closes the Monday prior to publication.' For a 2026-12-17 Thursday release that window is Mon 2026-12-07 through Mon 2026-12-14. Funding lapses 2026-12-12 absent new appropriations (government-funding-deadline-2026-12-11, high, estimate), so THREE of the window's eight calendar days sit inside a possible lapse — but only ONE of its six business days does, the closing Monday 12-14. The proposal's central claim therefore SURVIVES and SHRINKS: this is genuinely the pair's only December half with any post-cliff collection (Empire's published rule puts its bulk window at Dec 1-10, closing the day before), and the exposure is one business day out of six rather than a post-cliff snapshot. Impact LOW and symbols [] on grounds this ledger measures rather than assumes: a lapse leaves no detectable mark on this survey across the thirteen collection windows in 700 months that overlapped a federal funding gap (mean |monthly headline change| 9.21 vs 8.22 for the other 686, Welch t = 0.45 — the same null the Empire sibling found on n=4, at 3.25x the sample); the survey is a sub-state qualitative diffusion index of the Third District; and no house playbook is keyed to regional surveys. What earns the row is the morning's inversion: 2026-12-17 08:30 ET carries only housing-starts-2026-12-17 (Census, low, confirmed) and import-export-prices-2026-12-17 (BLS, low, estimate), and both are exactly what a lapse suspends — so on the lapse branch this Fed-funded survey is the ONLY 8:30 print of its morning, the mirror image of 2026-10-15 where retail sales and PPI made the pair unreadable. This is an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the ledger's stance is a permanent stand-aside.
